key_insight: Time-aware survival modeling from pre-treatment PET/CT projections improved lung cancer overall survival prediction, with different temporal designs better suited to early versus late follow-up.
clinical_relevance: This could help tailor risk stratification and follow-up planning in non-small cell lung cancer using imaging already collected before treatment.
method: Compared a baseline Time-Conditioned Survival model with two new approaches: Attention-guided Time-Conditioned Survival (ATCS) and Multi-Time Survival (MTS).
Used pre-treatment PET/CT data from 848 NSCLC patients, with 556 for development and 292 for held-out testing.
Evaluated time-dependent AUC every 6 months from 0.5 to 5 years and tested tumor-specific plus tissue-wise PET/CT feature inputs.
evidence_signal: ATCS and MTS both outperformed the baseline TCS model on the held-out test set, with mean AUCs of 0.794 and 0.793 versus 0.767.
watch_item: Performance was assessed retrospectively at a single cohort level, so external validation is needed before clinical use.
paper_title: Time-Conditioned and Multi-Time Survival Prediction from 2D PET/CT Projections in Lung Cancer
